info.name: PlanRadar's API Documentation Approval Requests V2 Tickets V2 API
Retrieve journals for all accessible tickets in a project

params.name: customer_id
params.description: Encoded customer ID

params.name: project_id
params.description: Encoded project ID

params.name: last_sync_date
params.description: ISO 8601 datetime. Only return journal entries created on or after this datetime. Use for incremental sync — pass the timestamp from your last successful sync.

params.name: prop_keys
params.description: Comma-separated list of journal_details.prop_key values to filter by (e.g. status_id, assigned_to_id). When provided, only journals with a matching detail row are returned.

params.name: page
params.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1.

params.name: pagesize
params.description: Number of journal entries per page. Default: 50. Maximum: 100 (server-enforced, values above 100 are clamped).

items.docs:
Retrieve journal entries for every ticket the caller can access within the given project,
in a single API call. Intended to replace individual `GET /tickets/{uuid}/journals` calls
during ERP sync integrations.

Counts as **1 API call**. Only returns journals from tickets the user has access to within
the specified project. Field-level and document permissions are respected. Each journal
entry includes `ticket-uuid` for mapping back to its ticket.

**Pagination:** default 50, max 100 (server-enfo

params.name: filter[status_id]
params.description:
Simple status ID filter. Use status codes: 1=Open, 2=In-Progress, 3=Resolved, 4=Feedback, 5=Closed, 6=Rejected. Example: filter[status_id]=1 - Structured filter parameter supporting multiple conditions and predicates. You can use either simple or advanced format.
Status ID Mapping: 1 (lm)=Open, 2 (ol)=In-Progress, 3 (ma)=Resolved, 4 (ex)=Feedback, 5 (gk)=Closed, 6 (ky)=Rejected
Simple Format: filter[{field}]={value} - Example: filter[status_id]=1
Advanced Format: filter[{field}][][predicate]={predicate}&filter[{field}][][value][]={value}
Supported Fields: status_id, priority-id, assigned-to-id, author-id, subject, created-at, due-date, etc.
Predicates: eq (equals), neq (not equals), in (in list), not_in (not in list), like (contains), not_like (not contains), between (range), has (has value), has_not (no value), le (less/equal), ge (greater/equal)
Examples:
• Simple: filter[status_id]=1 for filtering tickets with status 1
• Advanced: filter[status_id][][predicate]=in&filter[status_id][][value][]=1&filter[status_id][][value][]=2 for filtering tickets with status 1 or 2

params.name: filter[status_id]
params.description:
Simple status ID filter. Use status codes: 1=Open, 2=In-Progress, 3=Resolved, 4=Feedback, 5=Closed, 6=Rejected. Example: filter[status_id]=1 - Structured filter parameter supporting multiple conditions and predicates. You can use either simple or advanced format.
Status ID Mapping: 1 (lm)=Open, 2 (ol)=In-Progress, 3 (ma)=Resolved, 4 (ex)=Feedback, 5 (gk)=Closed, 6 (ky)=Rejected
Simple Format: `filter[{field}]={value}` - Direct field-value filtering
Advanced Format: `filter[{field}][][predicate]={predicate}&filter[{field}][][value][]={value}` - Complex filtering with predicates
Supported Fields: status_id, priority-id, assigned-to-id, author-id, subject, created-at, due-date, etc.
Predicates: eq (equals), neq (not equals), in (in list), not_in (not in list), like (contains), not_like (not contains), between (range), has (has value), has_not (no value), le (less/equal), ge (greater/equal)
Simple Format Examples:
• Filter by status: `filter[status_id]=1` (Open tickets)
• Filter by priority: `filter[priority-id]=3` (High priority)
• Multiple simple filters: `filter[status_id]=1&filter[priority-id]=3`
Advanced Format Examples:
• Status filtering with 'in': `filter[status_id][][predicate]=in&filter[status_id][][value][]=1&filter[status_id][][value][]=2`
• Text search with 'like': `filter[subject][][predicate]=like&filter[subject][][value][]=urgent`
• Date range filtering: `filter[created-at][][predicate]=between&filter[created-at][][value][]=2024-01-01&filter[created-at][][value][]=2024-12-31`
• Complex multiple conditions: `filter[status_id][][predicate]=eq&filter[status_id][][value][]=1&filter[priority-id][][predicate]=eq&filter[priority-id][][value][]=3`

Example: ticket_types_stats?apply_filter=jpg

Returns the current status of a bulk create job previously enqueued via the bulk_create endpoint. Poll this endpoint with the job_id returned by bulk_create to track progress and completion.

Status values
  • queued — the job has been enqueued but has not started yet.
  • processing — the job is currently creating tickets.
